newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 25.

text.p: The following are the highlights
of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
IRISH INDEPENDENT
- The Irish government will soon approve a major strategic plan to prepare Ireland for entry to the single currency even if Britain stays out.
- Ulster police launched a murder investigation on Monday after a Presbyterian minister died in hospital from horrific injuries he received in a loyalist paramilitary punishment beating.
- A sweeping plan aimed at gearing Ireland for the Information Society includes tax breaks for purchase of family computers, incentives for industry and a network of "cyber" schools and libraries.
IRISH TIMES

- Demands have been made for the immediate resignation of the governor of the Maze prison in Northern Ireland and for a full-scale public inquiry to be held after the discovery of an escape tunnel at the County Antrim jail.
- A Presbyterian minister has become the first person to die as a result of a so-called "punishment beating" in Northern
Ireland.
- Support for married and women priests is greater among Irish Catholics more than those in other church strongholds like Poland, Italy, Spain and the Philippines, according to a new
survey.
- The Irish pound has slipped back below 98 pence against sterling but has gained against the mark.
THE EXAMINER
- The Irish government on Monday launched its battle to save
Ireland's European Commission seat amid fears that its loss could jeopardise two billion punts a year in EU grant aid and farm supports.
- Irish police were reticent to comment on Monday on reports
that parts of the body of one of the victims of a double murder of two women, on March 6, were taken from the scene of the horror killings.
- Some of the Irish Republican Army's most dangerous activists
came within feat of tunnelling their way out of Europe's most secure prison.
